evidence_note: CNA and other credible follow-up reports confirm Yeo's laid off 25 employees at its Senoko facility as can manufacturing moved to Malaysia, so the previously rumored retrenchment has occurred. (~25 Singapore jobs)

Follow-up coverage confirms Standard Chartered announced a global plan to cut more than 7,000 corporate roles by 2030, but it remains a future/planned reduction and no Singapore-specific cut number is confirmed.
Follow-up coverage reports HSBC mulling a Singapore restructuring and hiring 100+ AI roles, while UK/global cuts are reported as plans; no Singapore job cuts or headcount are confirmed.

Follow-up coverage reports Daiso shuttering another Singapore store and analysts discussing cost pressures, but there is no confirmation that job cuts occurred or any Singapore headcount. The Kallang Wave Mall closure remains a planned store closure, so the layoff implication is still unconfirmed.

Follow-up coverage confirms the Plaza Singapura revamp and store closures, including GV's outlet closure, but does not confirm actual layoffs or a specific number of Singapore jobs cut. Retail workers' futures remain described as uncertain.

No Singapore-specific follow-up substantiates the reported 450 KPMG Singapore cuts under Project Vector; later coverage concerns KPMG Australia/UK/US layoffs rather than the Singapore rumor. The Singapore rumor therefore appears to have gone nowhere.

Follow-up reporting confirms Crisil extended the timeline for closing its Coalition Singapore subsidiary to July 2027 due to pending regulatory approvals, but it still only describes a future/anticipated closure rather than confirmed Singapore job cuts underway.
Follow-up coverage reports Yong He Eating House is closing, and OpenRice lists the outlet as closed, confirming the anticipated closure. No specific Singapore job-cut headcount was disclosed.

Follow-up reporting from Business Times, Ad Age and others continues to describe WPP's cuts as planned or anticipated, up to 1,000 roles by end-2026, rather than confirming completed layoffs. No company or government confirmation of Singapore-specific job cuts is provided.

Follow-up reporting in October 2026 states Omnicom's IPG-integration job cuts are near completion and the group is on course for a 15,000-role reduction, confirming the previously rumored cuts. No Singapore-specific headcount was provided.
Follow-up coverage from Reuters still reports that IG Group 'plans significant layoffs' rather than confirming that cuts have occurred or are underway. No specific Singapore headcount was provided.

Follow-up coverage from CNA, Reuters and Bloomberg reports that ExxonMobil expects or plans to cut up to about 500 Singapore staff by end-2027, with detailed planning still underway. This confirms the planned/anticipated nature of the reduction, but not that the Singapore job cuts have actually occurred or are actively underway.

Follow-up coverage reports Standard Chartered's official plan to cut more than 7,000 roles globally by 2030, but still frames the cuts as planned/anticipated rather than confirmed Singapore job losses. No Singapore-specific headcount is disclosed, and the Business Times notes Singapore may hire more wealth bankers.

Follow-up reporting confirms BioNTech is closing its Singapore vaccine plant, with People Matters Global reporting 85 employees impacted. Reuters later confirmed site closures in Germany and Singapore affecting 1,860 staff overall. (~85 Singapore jobs)

SI Group's own announcement and Business Times coverage confirm only a planned closure of the Singapore site in H2 2025, not that Singapore job cuts have actually occurred; later SI Group layoff coverage concerns Orangeburg, not Singapore.

Follow-up reporting confirms Oatly's Singapore plant closure resulted in layoffs, with 34 Oatly employees affected (plus 25 Yeo's workers, 59 total). Oatly also announced the asset-light supply chain move. (~34 Singapore jobs)

ExxonMobil itself confirmed it expects to cut 10-15% of its Singapore workforce — up to about 500 staff — by end-2027 (CNA, Reuters, Bloomberg, 1 Oct 2025), and Singapore's MOM issued a parliamentary answer on the ExxonMobil retrenchment in Nov 2025, confirming the cuts are real and underway. (~500 Singapore jobs)

SI Group's own announcement and Business Times coverage confirm only a planned closure of the Singapore manufacturing site in H2 2025; no follow-up evidence shows the Singapore job cuts actually occurred or gives a confirmed Singapore headcount.

Follow-up coverage confirms the Singapore closures and that former True Fitness/True Yoga staff, freelancers, and employees were affected and are receiving job-matching help. No exact Singapore layoff headcount is clearly confirmed.

Follow-up reporting confirms True Fitness and True Yoga shut their Singapore operations, with former employees receiving job-matching support. No single precise Singapore headcount is confirmed, though reports mention more than 200 affected staff and freelancers.

Follow-up coverage (TelecomLead, dated Dec 2011) only restates Photronics' announcement that it will stop photomask manufacturing at its Singapore unit; no source confirms the halt was completed or that Singapore jobs were actually cut, and no headcount is disclosed.

Follow-up coverage confirms a restructuring exercise at BBC News Singapore Bureau and that staff were asked to reapply, but no report confirms actual Singapore job cuts or a headcount. The situation remains an anticipated/unconfirmed restructuring outcome.
Standard Chartered officially announced plans to cut more than 7,000 roles globally by 2030, with follow-up reporting confirming the AI-driven job cuts; no Singapore-specific headcount was provided.

Follow-up coverage (CNA, Straits Times, Mothership, Inside Retail, 8days) all report the same announcement that Cinnabon's last Singapore outlet at Ion Orchard will shut on Sep 22, 2026 — the closure is still ahead and no actual job cuts or headcount numbers are confirmed.

SI Group and Business Times reported the planned closure of the Singapore manufacturing site, but the follow-up evidence only confirms the plan/anticipated closure, not actual Singapore job cuts or completion. Later SI Group layoff coverage concerns Orangeburg, not Singapore.

Follow-up reports confirm Cinnabon announced it will close its last ION Orchard outlet on 22 Sep 2026, but the closure and any job losses are still future and no Singapore headcount or actual cuts are confirmed. The event therefore remains planned/anticipated rather than confirmed as happened.

Follow-up reporting confirms Jumbo Seafood's flagship East Coast outlet closed after 39 years, substantiating the previously rumored closure and implied job losses. No Singapore headcount was disclosed.

Follow-up coverage (CNA, Straits Times, Mothership, 8days) uniformly reports the announced closure of the last Ion Orchard outlet with a future last day of Sep 22, 2026, so the implied job losses are still anticipated rather than confirmed as executed; no Singapore headcount is stated.

CNA Lifestyle confirms Cinnabon Singapore announced the closure of its last Ion Orchard outlet, with last day on Sep 22, substantiating the reported shutdown and implied job losses; no Singapore headcount was disclosed.

Follow-up coverage repeats that Tash Tish Tosh is seeking public help to save its last outlet, but no report confirms actual Singapore job cuts or a headcount. The evidence remains an unconfirmed closure/survival story rather than confirmed layoffs.

Follow-up reporting confirms True Fitness and True Yoga closed in Singapore and employees were affected, with job-matching assistance for former staff; RSM also notes both companies are in provisional liquidation. No exact Singapore headcount is confirmed in the evidence.

Follow-up coverage (Reuters, BBC, Bloomberg, Straits Times) consistently frames DBS's 4,000 reduction as a forward-looking, attrition-driven plan to shrink contract/temp roles over three years, not cuts already executed; later CNA reporting (Nov 2025) says DBS will focus on reskilling staff rather than cutting jobs, and the 4,000 figure remains a bank-wide/global target rather than a confirmed Singapore headcount reduction.

Follow-up coverage (e.g. CNA Nov 2025 reporting DBS/UOB will focus on reskilling rather than cutting, and BT's April 2026 piece on combined DBS/OCBC/UOB workforce being down 2.6%) shows the workforce narrative evolving, but no report confirms that the specific ~4,000 contract/temporary roles projected by the CEO were actually removed or are actively being cut. The figure remains a group-wide, forward-looking projection rather than a confirmed Singapore-specific layoff, so it stays rumored.
